Subject: Order form pricing exhibit — a couple mapping clarifications

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick follow-up: we reviewed the Stratus redline notes against the order form and found two places where the exhibit language/definitions don't map to the operational billing lanes (we think this is causing the caps/floors to appear broader than intended).

Top items:
- Exhibit A, section "Fee Bands" references "Service Unit" but the order schedule lists "Token Units" and the conversion rule is missing. We should align on the conversion (e.g., 1 Service Unit = 2500 tokens) or explicitly map the metric.
- Exhibit C cap/floor table uses quarterly aggregations, but your procurement redline suggests monthly true-ups. We need to decide cadence — monthly true-up will change the effective floor behavior for month-to-month spikes.

I attached a working PDF with inline comments (redwood_revised-orderform-20260320.pdf) and a copy of the redlines you sent so we stay in sync. Can you confirm whether Stratus prefers monthly true-ups (and if so, are you okay with a 90-day smoothing to avoid over-triggering the floor)?

Proposed next step: if you're open, I'll loop in Marissa and Karthik from my team to produce a brief markup that preserves your risk profile but keeps our billing mapping consistent.

Thanks,
Sean

Thanks, Sean — appreciate the fast turnaround and annotated order form. We attached our consolidated redline set (Stratus_Pricing_Redlines_v3.pdf) — highlights below: 

- We flagged the Service Unit vs Token Unit mismatch. Our legal insists that the metric in Exhibit A be the measured metric used in billing; if Redwood wants to keep an internal conversion, it must be included as a defined conversion table in the exhibit.
- Procurement prefers monthly true-ups (we reconcile monthly internally). However, we can consider a 60–90 day smoothing window as a compromise; need your proposal in writing.
- We also requested an explicit protection for sudden, month-long traffic drops that could otherwise trigger a floor obligation (we proposed a 30-day exclusion for force-majeure-like anomalies).

We are in contract week for Stratus; Emily and I need a firm position today so our GC can review. Can Marissa/Karthik propose wording that: (1) defines the metric mapping, (2) specifies the true-up cadence and smoothing, and (3) provides an operational exclusion for anomalous short-lived drops?

Marissa / Karthik / Irene — forwarding Stratus's redlines (attached). Key asks from Stratus: define the Service Unit ↔ Token mapping in the exhibit, accept monthly true-ups or propose smoothing cadence, and add a short-term drop exclusion clause. They need our wording today for legal review.

My recommended approach:
1) Add a new table to Exhibit A called "Unit Definitions & Conversions" with the explicit conversion factor and a note that the invoice will show Token Units; the Service Unit nomenclature will be deprecated.
2) Offer monthly true-ups with a 75-day smoothing window (compromise between their 60 and our operational batching).

If you agree, can one of you draft the exhibit language and we send back to Alex + Emily with the revised PDF (redwood_revised-orderform-20260320.pdf) plus a short cover note?

Subject: RE: Order form pricing exhibit — a couple mapping clarifications

Alex / Emily — thanks for the clear redline. Per Sean's ask, we've drafted three short edits below and attached an updated order form PDF with inline wording (redwood_revised-orderform-20260320.pdf). High level summary: 

1) Unit mapping table (Exhibit A, new section): 1 Service Unit = 2,500 tokens. Invoice metric: Token Units. Conversion table included in the exhibit so it is contractual.

2) True-up cadence (Exhibit C, paragraph 2): Monthly billing/usage reporting with a 75-day rolling smoothing window applied for floor/cap calculation (smoothing calculated as the average of the most recent three monthly invoiced usages). Language provided to preserve Stratus's reconciliation cadence while limiting month-to-month floor volatility.

3) Operational anomaly carve-out (Exhibit C, paragraph 4): A 30-day exclusion for documented platform incidents, force majeure, or upstream provider outages; exclusion requires written notice within 15 days of the incident and a joint post-mortem within 45 days. Carve-out does not apply to planned maintenance.

We believe this set keeps Stratus's monthly reconciliation preference intact while protecting Redwood from unnecessary floor triggers during short spikes/dips. If that works, we'll produce a clean PDF and also a redline for your GC. If your GC has any narrow phrasing requests, please send them back and we'll try to resolve without changing economic terms.

Proposed next step: Alex, if we get a quick ack today, I'll upload the clean order form to the Drive link and share a DocuSign packet with the revised Exhibit A + C attached. Otherwise we can schedule a 20-min call to finalize.
